subject: Auth anomaly notification — request for IR plan + evidence bundle
messages:
From: Allen Torres <allen.torres@finops-guardian.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Nguyen <laura.nguyen@finops-guardian.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious auth events detected — request for IR plan + evidence

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

We flagged several anomalous authentication events targeting our integration with Redwood on Feb 27–28 (multiple failed token retries from two IP ranges, followed by a brief successful login from a new region). Our security and compliance teams are preparing for a SOC 2 readiness audit and need a few items from Redwood to complete our evidence package:

- The current Incident Response Plan (IRP) and point-of-contact for incident escalations.
- A curated, minimally redacted sample of authentication logs for 2027-02-27 and 2027-02-28 (timestamps, event types, IPs, user identifiers).
- Any post-incident notes or initial forensics you have if you performed an internal triage.

We appreciate this is sensitive — please mark any artifacts as Confidential and provide guidance on redaction for PII. Ideally we would receive the package by EOD Tue 2027-03-09 to feed into our audit evidence binder. If there are contractual disclosures or SLAs we should be aware of, flag them.

Thanks — this is time-sensitive for our audit kickoff.

Allen Torres
Director, Security Operations
FinOps Guardian
allen.torres@finops-guardian.com
+1 415-555-0134

[Attachment: screenshot-alert-20270227.png (PNG, 120KB)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Allen Torres <allen.torres@finops-guardian.com>, Laura Nguyen <laura.nguyen@finops-guardian.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious auth events detected — request for IR plan + evidence

Allen — thanks for the heads up and the detail. We take these reports seriously.

Short answers up front: yes, we have a documented IRP and we can assemble a curated evidence bundle for the date range you specified. Before I pull logs, two quick clarifying points so we scope the deliverable correctly:

1) Scope: do you need only the integration-related auth events (API keys / service accounts tied to your org) or all auth attempts that reference your tenant id?
2) Redaction: confirm whether FinOps Guardian's compliance team requires IPs fully redacted, partially redacted (e.g., last octet masked), or IPs preserved. We will default to masking last octet unless you ask otherwise.

I've looped Neha (Security Engineering) to coordinate log extraction and any forensics notes. Marissa — looping you to keep the account team aware of timelines/communication.

Plan: we will (a) share a current IRP PDF, (b) provide a sample CSV with the requested auth events and a short forensic summary, and (c) deliver these via a secure shared Drive link (or S3 pre-signed object, whichever you prefer). Target delivery: Tue 2027-03-09 EOD as requested.

If you confirm scope and redaction preference I will trigger the extraction and get Neha to add any post-triage commentary.

— Priyom
Priyom Das

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious auth events detected — request for IR plan + evidence

Thanks Priyom — quick notes from Security Engineering on what we can produce and recommended redaction: 

- We retain auth telemetry for 90 days in production by default; the requested dates fall within that window.
- We can export a scoped CSV of events filtered to your tenant id and the API keys associated with your account. That will include timestamp (UTC), event_type, src_ip, user_agent, and tenant_id.
- Recommended redaction: mask the final octet of IPv4 addresses (e.g., 198.51.100.xxx) and hash any user identifiers (we can provide the hash algorithm if you need deterministic mapping for internal correlation).
- We will include an abbreviated forensic notes file describing initial triage steps (what we looked at, whether we observed abnormal behavior outside the auth attempts, and any mitigation steps taken).

Attachment: audit-logs-sample-20270227-28.csv (sample extract, sanitized).

Allen — please confirm whether masking last octet + hashed user ids is acceptable. Also confirm preferred delivery method: secure Drive link (we will set viewer restrictions and expiration) or pre-signed S3 (we can provide shorter-lived access).

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Allen — thanks for raising. A couple customer-facing notes from the account team:

- We will mark the artifacts "Confidential — for FinOps Guardian audit use only." Please treat the Drive link as restricted; do not circulate publicly without written consent from Redwood and FinOps Guardian.
- If you plan to publish a public post-incident summary, please loop us before publishing so we can align messaging. We prefer to avoid any public disclosure until both parties agree on timing and redactions.

Also, if this audit triggers contract-level requirements (SLA credits, formal incident report), Allen please flag which procurement / legal contacts should be included and we will escalate.

Marissa Cole

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Evidence package and IRP delivery — FinOps Guardian (Feb 27–28)

Allen / Laura — deliverables attached and links below per scope agreed:

1) IRP_Redwood_v2.1.pdf — our current incident response plan (internal contact list redacted for customer distribution).
2) evidence-package-20270309.zip — curated bundle containing:
   - audit-logs-sample-20270227-28.csv (IP masked by last octet, user ids hashed)
   - forensic-notes-20270306.txt (initial triage summary; no internal-only debug traces)
   - preservation memo (notes on log retention and chain-of-custody)
3) Shared Drive link (secure, expires 30 days): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/Redwood-FinOps-IR-evidence

Notes / summary:
- We observed the sequence Allen described: a set of failed token attempts from two ASN blocks, followed by a single successful API auth from an EU-based IP at 2027-02-28T03:42:17Z. At the time of triage we rotated the associated API key and flagged the tenant for elevated monitoring. No evidence of data exfiltration was found in the service logs we could access.
- We recommend FinOps Guardian rotate any customer-side keys you believe may have been exposed and rotate integration secrets on your side as a precaution.

If SOC Audit needs a direct S3 transfer or a signed statement from Redwood Security, tell us the required format and we'll escalate to our compliance team.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the artifacts (I can book Neha and Marissa).

— Priyom
